articles.full_text:
कानपुर में दिवाली के बाद बढ़ेगी ठंड, पारे में गिरावट और प्रदूषण का खतरा
दिवाली के बाद कानपुर में तापमान में दो डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिरावट आने की संभावना है, जिससे सुबह-शाम ठंड बढ़ेगी। ...और पढ़ें
HighLights
दिवाली के बाद कानपुर में तापमान दो डिग्री गिरेगा।
सुबह-शाम ठंड बढ़ेगी, दिन में धूप बनी रहेगी।
धीमी हवा से प्रदूषण बढ़ने की आशंका, सावधानी जरूरी।
जागरण संवाददाता, कानपुर। दिन में तेज धूप और सुबह-शाम की ठंडक के बीच मौसम का मिजाज बदलने लगा है। दिवाली के बाद तापमान में दो डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिरावट आने के आसार हैं। शनिवार को अधिकतम तापमान 30.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस दर्ज किया गया, जो सामान्य से 0.3 डिग्री अधिक रहा। वहीं, न्यूनतम तापमान 15.4 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहा, इसमें भी 0.8 डिग्री की बढ़ोतरी दर्ज की गई। दिन में धूप के कारण गर्मी का अहसास हुआ, जबकि सुबह और शाम ठंडक बनी रही।
मौसम विशेषज्ञ डा. एसएन सुनील पांडेय ने बताया कि पहाड़ों से आने वाली उत्तर-पश्चिमी शुष्क और ठंडी हवा का लगातार प्रवाह नहीं बन पा रहा है। इन हवा की निरंतरता बनने पर ही ठंड का असर स्थिर होगा। फिलहाल दिन में धूप निकलने से अधिकतम तापमान में ज्यादा गिरावट की संभावना नहीं है। ऊपरी वातावरण में नमी के कारण कहीं-कहीं ऊंचे बादल छा सकते हैं, जिससे धूप की तीव्रता कुछ कम रहेगी।
शाम को बादलों की मौजूदगी तापमान में गिरावट को थाम सकती है। दूसरी ओर, हवा की रफ्तार महज 1.5 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटा रहने से प्रदूषक तत्व वातावरण में ठहर रहे हैं। शनिवार को अधिकतम सापेक्षिक आर्द्रता 94 और न्यूनतम 44 प्रतिशत दर्ज की गई। हवा की दिशा उत्तर-पश्चिमी रही। धीमी हवा और तापमान में उतार-चढ़ाव के बीच रात में धुंध की मोटी परत छाने की आशंका है। ऐसे में सांस संबंधी बीमारियों से जूझ रहे लोगों और बुजुर्गों को विशेष सावधानी बरतने की जरूरत है।

articles.title: Fadnavis celebrates Diwali with Narkhed farmers, vows more drought-relief measures - The Times of India

articles.full_text:
Nagpur: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday assured farmers in drought-hit regions of Maharashtra that his govt stands firmly behind them and promised further relief measures to help them overcome the agrarian crisis.
Celebrating Diwali with farmers at Lohari Sawanga village in Narkhed taluka of Nagpur district, Fadnavis said govt was committed to supporting cultivators through financial assistance, agricultural infrastructure and water conservation initiatives.
Fadnavis stayed at the house of farmer Rambhau Balpande, where he shared a traditional meal prepared by the women of the family. Sitting on the floor, the CM had a village-style dinner comprising bhakri, chapatis, potato and brinjal curry, bharit, dal and rice.
Balpande highlighted the financial distress confronting farmers, inadequate irrigation facilities, low water availability and mounting cultivation costs. He said farmers were struggling to meet agricultural expenses and repay loans, with a poor monsoon and crop losses making the situation worse.
The CM also discussed difficulties faced by orange and sweet lime growers in the Katol-Narkhed belt, who suffered losses due to Bangladesh’s restrictions on imports.
He said a major project coming up at Mihan would create opportunities for processing these fruits and provide an alternative market for farmers.
Acknowledging the difficult agricultural conditions this year, Fadnavis said less rainfall and adverse weather conditions had caused extensive damage to crops, leaving farmers facing severe financial distress. “Soyabean crops failed to develop pods, while cotton and other crops suffered significant losses. Several areas were additionally grappling with shortages of drinking water and fodder for cattle,” he said.
Listing the steps taken by his govt, Fadnavis said loan waiver benefits had already been deposited into accounts of 21 lakh farmers, while the process was underway to extend the benefit to nearly 55 lakh farmers. Additionally, advance assistance of Rs5,000 had been deposited into the accounts of around 1.5 crore farmers. Govt would soon begin disbursing drought-related financial assistance, he added.
Highlighting another major relief measure, Fadnavis said the state govt had decided to waive farmers’ electricity bills completely, involving an expenditure of around Rs58,000 crore.
On his decision to celebrate Diwali with farmers, the CM said he wanted to boost their morale through direct interaction.
Invoking the teachings of Rashtrasant Tukdoji Maharaj, Fadnavis said his
Gramgeeta offered a roadmap for rural prosperity, covering agriculture, cleanliness, economic development and community participation. He said the saint’s devotional compositions and teachings had the power to give people strength during difficult circumstances.
Referring to the need for long-term drought preparedness, Fadnavis said govt would undertake extensive water conservation works, including repairs to old lakes and check dams, construction of new water conservation structures and improvement of farm access roads under the state’s
pandan road scheme.
The CM said preparing water conservation infrastructure before the arrival of the next monsoon would be crucial to helping drought-affected areas overcome recurring water shortages. “The govt would also organise health camps and facilitate surgeries and other medical interventions in different locations to ensure that people did not face difficulties due to a lack of money,” he said.
Several schemes were already being implemented and more initiatives would be announced to address the difficulties faced by farmers and rural communities. Reiterating that the entire govt was committed to helping the farmers, he appealed to villagers to face the crisis collectively. He also said govt would permit digging of irrigation wells wherever feasible to help farmers tackle the water crisis.
Fadnavis was accompanied by revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule, MLAs Charansingh Thakur, Ashish Deshmukh, MLC Rajiv Potdar, district collector Kumar Ashirwad and ZP chief executive officer Vinayak Mahamuni.

articles.full_text:
HYDERABAD: Hyderabad is likely to see partly cloudy skies and hazy conditions during the morning on Saturday, November 7, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Hyderabad. The maximum and minimum temperatures are expected to be around 32°C and 20°C, respectively, with north-easterly winds at 4–8 kmph.
The IMD has forecast light to moderate rain or thundershowers at isolated places across Telangana on November 7 and 8. A yellow warning has been issued for thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds of 30–40 kmph in nine districts on November 7. The bulletin does not list a separate thunderstorm warning for Hyderabad.
Hyderabad weather today: Will it rain on November 7?
The city is likely to have partly cloudy skies, with haze during the morning. The local forecast gives temperatures of around 32°C maximum and 20°C minimum, with north-easterly surface winds at 4–8 kmph.
The bulletin does not specifically forecast rain for Hyderabad city in its local 24-hour outlook. However, it forecasts isolated light to moderate rain or thundershowers in Telangana as a whole.
The reported observations for Hyderabad were a maximum temperature of 32°C, minimum of 20.2°C, relative humidity of 79% and no rainfall (0.0 mm).
Hyderabad weather tomorrow: What to expect on November 8
The city’s 48-hour outlook continues to indicate partly cloudy skies and morning haze, with temperatures likely to remain around 32°C and 20°C. North-easterly winds are expected at 4–8 kmph.
Across Telangana, isolated light to moderate rain or thundershowers are very likely on November 8. The bulletin lists no weather warning for the state on that day.

No warnings have been listed for November 8 to 13.

November 8 – Isolated light to moderate rain or thundershowers

The supplied bulletin provides a local Hyderabad outlook for the next 24 and 48 hours, but does not include a zone-wise city forecast for the following five days.
IMD advisory: Precautions during thunderstorms
Residents in districts under the yellow warning should move indoors when thunderstorms approach and avoid standing under trees or near exposed electrical poles. People should stay away from open areas, water bodies and metal structures during lightning.
The IMD describes the warning as applying to isolated places. It does not issue a heavy-rain warning in the supplied bulletin.
Why is Telangana likely to receive rain?
The IMD said an upper-air cyclonic circulation over east Telangana and adjoining Coastal Andhra Pradesh, at 4.5 km above mean sea level, had become less marked by 05.30 IST on November 7.
